body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「一個 assistant 經常答錯。你幾時會 fine-tune，幾時會先修 system？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「資料愈多愈好，所以我會 fine-tune 一個更強 model。」

Fine-tuning 可以令一個 model 對穩定、重複而且可定義的 behaviour 更一致；它不能補一份未入 context 的新政策、修一個錯 permission filter，或把含糊 user request 變成可靠決定。先把『答錯』拆開，才不會用訓練成本掩蓋 ingestion、retrieval、prompt contract、tool route 或 workflow ownership 的問題。

## 先畫 failure taxonomy，不要先買資料

拿固定 cases 把錯誤分成幾類：缺 source、取錯 source、source 已到但沒有跟隨、格式不穩、穩定分類邊界模糊、工具選錯、或系統本來應該拒絕。若內容日日更新，問題是 freshness；若角色看見不該看的文件，問題是 authorisation；若 output 少一個 required field，先收緊 schema 和 validator。只有當同一種已定義 task 在乾淨、穩定的 input 上反覆失敗，而且較簡單的 system fix 已被比較，才開始評估 fine-tune。

## Fine-tune 要解一個明確、可維護的 task

例如將已授權的 synthetic support note 分成幾個固定 routing class，且 class definition 幾個月內不會改。你仍要有 baseline：prompted model、rule 或人工 checklist；還要有 time-safe train/validation/test split、資料卡、label owner、刪除／更正路徑和保留的 hard cases。不要把 model 當作資料庫：事實、政策、私隱和權限應留在 versioned source 和 service control，而不是烙進 weights。

## 比較不是只看一個分數

同一個 fixture suite 量 baseline 和 fine-tuned candidate 的 class-level errors、calibration、refusal／handoff、latency、cost proxy 和 reviewer 接受率。加入一個 counterexample：candidate 在常見 class 變好，卻把罕見但高風險 case 分錯；或新政策一改，兩個 model 都答舊事實。第一種要求調資料、threshold 或留人工；第二種說明應修 source path 而非再訓練。

## 面試時怎樣說出判斷

可以說：『我會先把錯誤定位成資料、檢索、contract、權限或穩定 task behaviour。Fine-tune 只處理最後一種，而且要比 baseline、保存 label 定義和退出路徑。』這能說清它解到甚麼，也說清它絕對不解甚麼。

## 讓 reviewer 檢查的 evidence

- **工程：** failure taxonomy、data card、label guide、time-safe split、baseline/candidate matrix、case-level regression report。
- **交付：** label owner、資料可否使用、何時要更新／撤回、誰 review 高風險 class，以及哪些 request 必須交接。
- **風險：** 一個明確寫出的 non-fit case，例如需要當日政策或授權判斷，證明你沒有把 fine-tune 當萬用修復。

> 答对一半的答案：“数据越多越好，所以我会 fine-tune 一个更强 model。”

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “An assistant is often wrong. When would you fine-tune, and when would you repair the system first?”
>
> Half-right answer: “More data is always better, so I would fine-tune a stronger model.”

Fine-tuning can make a model more consistent at stable, repetitive, well-defined behaviour. It cannot supply a new policy missing from context, repair a bad permission filter, or turn an ambiguous user request into a reliable decision. Split ‘wrong answer’ into causes before using training cost to hide a problem in ingestion, retrieval, prompt contract, tool routing or workflow ownership.

## Draw the failure taxonomy before buying data

Use fixed cases to classify failures: missing source, wrong source, source present but not followed, unstable format, fuzzy boundary of a stable class, wrong tool choice, or a request the system should refuse. Daily-changing content is a freshness problem. A role seeing an impermissible document is authorisation. A missing required output field calls for a stricter schema and validator. Evaluate fine-tuning only when the same defined task repeatedly fails on clean, stable input and simpler system fixes have been compared.

## Fine-tune one explicit, maintainable task

For example, route authorised synthetic support notes into fixed classes whose definitions will not change for months. You still need a baseline: a prompted model, rule, or human checklist; a time-safe train/validation/test split; a data card; a label owner; deletion/correction paths; and preserved hard cases. Do not use weights as a database. Facts, policy, privacy and permissions belong in versioned sources and service controls.

## A comparison is not one score

On the same fixture suite, compare baseline and fine-tuned candidate by class-level errors, calibration, refusal/handoff, latency, cost proxy and reviewer acceptance. Include a counterexample: the candidate improves common classes but misroutes a rare high-risk case; or a new policy changes and both models repeat old facts. The first may call for data, threshold or a human. The second says repair the source path, not train again.

## State the judgement in an interview

‘I first localise the error to data, retrieval, contract, permission or stable task behaviour. Fine-tuning only addresses the last category, and it must be compared to a baseline with a preserved label definition and exit route.’ This makes clear both what it solves and what it never solves.

## Evidence a reviewer can inspect

- **Engineering:** failure taxonomy, data card, label guide, time-safe split, baseline/candidate matrix and case-level regression report.
- **Delivery:** label owner, data-use boundary, update/withdrawal trigger, reviewer for high-risk classes, and requests that require handoff.
- **Risk:** one explicit non-fit case, such as a request requiring today’s policy or an authorisation judgement, showing that fine-tuning is not a universal repair.

## Further reading

[Why did a stable prompt fail when the context changed?](/en/interview-lab/prompt-contracts-need-an-acceptance-test), [Data drift is not just a retraining trigger](/en/interview-lab/data-drift-is-not-just-a-retraining-trigger), and [A label definition can change the model](/en/interview-lab/a-label-definition-can-change-the-model).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. Datasets, labels, models and comparisons are synthetic teaching material; they do not represent training data, customer data or a production model.
